abstract: New York Times investigation (reported by Gizmodo, October 21, 2025) using internal Amazon documents and interviews finds Amazon crossed 1 million deployed robots by mid-2025 and set an internal target to automate 75% of its operations. Executives told the board that automation could prevent hiring 600,000+ workers as sales double by 2033, saving ~30 cents per shipped item.
keyFindings: 1 million robots deployed globally at Amazon by mid-2025
Amazon robotics team internal goal: automate 75% of company operations
Executives project avoiding 600,000+ new hires by 2033 through automation, as sales are expected to double
By 2027, automation team expects to avoid hiring 160,000+ US workers Amazon would otherwise need
Estimated savings: ~30 cents on every item Amazon packs and delivers
methodology: New York Times investigation reviewed internal Amazon documents and conducted interviews with current and former employees. Numbers reflect internal executive-level projections and hiring-avoidance targets, not observed displacement.
qualifiers: 'Avoided hires' is a counterfactual metric, not observed layoffs — Amazon has continued growing headcount overall. Internal projections may not materialize as stated; leaked plans routinely change.
